ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision); Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Market Entities; and, to the extent Taiwan-origin evidence is relied upon, Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act and Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Terrorism Financing by Enterprises.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign shareholder/investor (corporate existence certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the investor's home jurisdiction (for Taiwan-origin investor, the Ministry of Economic Affairs commercial registry or other applicable statutory registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state path: notarization by a qualified notary, followed by issuance of an Apostille Certificate by the designated Competent Authority of the issuing state; consular legalization is prohibited in series. Non-member state path, including Taiwan-origin certificates where consular legalization applies: notarization by a local notary, certification by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, followed by legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; no Apostille is to be added. Select exclusively the path for the document's country of issuance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (recent registrar certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states, notarize the certificate then have the competent state authority issue an Apostille; do not add consular legalization. For non-convention states and Taiwan-origin documents subject to consular legalization, notarize, have the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing jurisdiction authenticate, then obtain consular legalization from the PRC Embassy/Consulate. Never chain an Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the CN WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors (or equivalent corporate governing body) of the foreign shareholder/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the board resolution is signed in an Apostille Convention state, the original signed resolution must be notarized and then apostilled by the state Competent Authority; consular legalization is inapplicable. If signed in a non-member state or under Taiwan cross-strait practice, notarize the board resolution, authenticate it with the local competent authority, and submit it for consular legalization at the competent Chinese consular post. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be performed sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum and Articles) of the foreign shareholder/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or certified director/company secretary of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the file copy and affix a Hague Apostille from the issuing state's designated authority. Consular path: notarize, authenticate through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize through the PRC Embassy/Consulate. Use only the path that applies to the territory of issuance; Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and cannot be chained together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (from the foreign shareholder's relationship bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder's relationship bank (bank officer authorized to issue KYC references)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille member state: the bank reference letter must be notarized and then apostilled by the member state's Competent Authority; no consular action. For a non-member state or Taiwan-origin letter subject to consular legalization: notarize the bank officer's signature, authenticate the notarized letter with the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize through the PRC Embassy/Consulate before submission. Avoid any sequence that combines Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all ultimate beneficial owners, direct and indirect shareholders above 25%, legal representatives, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and high-risk counterparties connected to the ISIC 4669 petrochemical polymer trading book. Screening must include: (i) domestic and international PEP databases, including political exposure of PRC state-owned entities and foreign government officials; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists and UN sanctions resolutions; (iv) EU, UK HMT, and PRC MPS/CSRC sanctions lists; (v) adverse media and enforcement actions; and (vi) bank-issued negative news and trade-based money-laundering red flags. Enhanced Due Diligence requires source of wealth and source of funds evidence for any PEP or sanctioned-nexus transaction, with re-screening every 90 days. For petrochemical wholesale, additional screening of shipping companies, insurers, freight forwarders, and end buyers must be performed to detect front companies, shell companies, price manipulation, and diversion to sanctioned jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Reservation System via the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The PRC WFOE name must be registered in simplified Chinese characters following the four-tier structure: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry characteristics (wholesale of petrochemical polymers) plus limited liability company. The foreign shareholder's translated name must be consistent with the notarized certificate of incorporation; phonetic pinyin transliteration is used when converting foreign entity names; English-only names, traditional Chinese names, and names with letters, numerals, or symbols are generally prohibited unless approved under special industrial policies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration with the higher-level market regulatory authority within 60 days of receiving the written rejection, or initiate administrative litigation before the competent People's Court within 6 months. In parallel, the applicant should file a modified name application that removes the offending sensitive token, adds a more distinctive two-character trade name, and preserves priority; attach the legalized Certificate of Incorporation and any prior trademark registration. The registry must respond within 10 working days to the appeal, and if the rejection was due to similarity with an existing registered name, the applicant should immediately reserve an alternative name online and may request a formal written explanation to support further legal challenge.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this WFOE. PRC Company Law and market entity registration rules require a fixed and lawful physical business address in the same municipal area as the registration authority. A virtual office, commercial mailbox, co-working nominal desk, or domicile-only address will be rejected by the municipal SAMR for the petrochemical wholesale business scope, and banks will decline account opening because the ISIC 4669 trading entity must present actual premises for KYC and tax invoice control. The State Taxation Administration also requires a lease-backed physical place for VAT general taxpayer registration and on-site inspection on first issuance of invoices; therefore, a fully operational office with actual employees and records is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: high, with a 60-75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the municipal SAMR and local tax authority within the first 12 months of registration. Checklist for inspection readiness: (1) matching company nameplate; (2) occupied desks and at least one local manager present; (3) original lease, rent receipts, and landlord's title certificate on site; (4) utility bills and internet contract in the WFOE name; (5) board-book, articles of association, seal, and bank KYC package; (6) invoice books, tax filing records, and contract files; (7) evidence of physical commerce, including LC, bills of lading, customs declarations, and polymer supplier/end-buyer purchase orders; (8) no sham signage or employee artifacts. Failure on items (1), (3), or (5) can trigger de-registration and permanent blacklisting.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), as amended and consolidated, particularly Articles 6, 7, 8, 17, 18, 20, 128, 156, 161, 172, 192, 193, 202, 204, and 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 10, and 12; Regulations Governing the Investment in Taiwan by Foreign Nationals; Regulations Governing the Investment in Taiwan by Mainland People, where applicable; and the Regulations Governing Company Registration by the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, operating through the Company Registration Electronization Portal; Investment Commission, MOEA, for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form (公司登記申請書), together with the Articles of Incorporation, first board resolution, capital verification report, and prescribed attachments submitted to the Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required under the Taiwan Company Act, but the paid-in capital must be adequate for the stated business scope. The foreign investor must obtain prior Investment Commission approval, remit the subscribed capital into a Taiwan bank account in the name of the proposed WFOE, and cause a Taiwan-certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report under Company Act Article 7. No general escrow or blocked-account mandate is imposed by Taiwan law; however, the remitted capital may not be withdrawn or deployed for operating expenses before incorporation is registered and the capital verification is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the Board of Directors of [Company Name], duly convened as the first board meeting after the formation meeting, with all directors present, acting under the Taiwan Company Act and the Foreign Investment Act, as follows: (1) Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The Board confirms that the authorized share capital of the Company is [number] ordinary shares with a par value of New Taiwan Dollars ten per share, and that the total authorized capital is [amount] New Taiwan Dollars. The Board approves the subscription agreement executed by the initial subscribers and directs the chairperson to issue the subscribed paid-in shares in accordance with the capital subscription schedule, to procure remittance of the foreign investment capital from the overseas investor, and to engage a Taiwan-certified public accountant to prepare the capital verification report required by Article 7 of the Taiwan Company Act. (2) Registered Office Adoption. The Board designates [address], Taiwan, as the registered office and principal place of business of the Company, and authorizes the president to execute any lease, occupancy consent, use agreement, or landlord consent required to prove the Company’s right to use such premises, and to deliver such evidence to the competent authority in connection with the incorporation application. (3) Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the Company to open, maintain, and operate demand deposit, general foreign currency, trade finance, and letter-of-credit accounts at [Bank Name], Taiwan. The Board approves the account signatory mandate requiring the joint signature of any two of the following persons: [Chief Financial Officer], [Chairperson], and [Treasury Manager], and authorizes such persons to execute account opening agreements, banking forms, SWIFT instructions, LC applications, foreign exchange contracts, and all compliance certifications, including anti-money laundering and knowledge-of-customer declarations. (4) Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [Name] as chairperson of the board and statutory representative, [Name] as president, [Name] as chief financial officer, and [Name] as corporate secretary, each to hold office until the next annual shareholders meeting and until successors are elected and qualified. The Board directs the corporate secretary to file all consents to act, definitive registers, and statutory declarations required by law. (5) Governance and Delegation. The Board approves the adoption of the corporate seal specimen, the delegation of authority matrix, segregation of duties, and the execution of the Articles of Incorporation by the designated incorporators. The chairperson is expressly authorized to sign, submit, and receive all regulatory filings, including the Company Registration Application Form, and to retain legal counsel to complete the incorporation process. (6) Compliance. The Board directs management to implement anti-money laundering and sanctions screening controls applicable to the SWIFT and irrevocable letter-of-credit payment rails, to maintain beneficial ownership records, and to present a compliance review at the next board meeting. This resolution is effective immediately, is final until amended by a subsequent board resolution, and all third parties are entitled to rely on it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Seal Creation, Bank Account Activation, and Work Plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau under the Ministry of Finance, the municipal commerce or licensing office, the local fire department for any warehouse premises, and a licensed Taiwan commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the MOEA issues the establishment certificate, the company must obtain the official corporate chop and open a corporate bank operating account. The company must register as a profit-seeking enterprise with the local National Taxation Bureau for business tax and corporate income tax, obtain its unified invoice registration, and apply for any required customs registration if the company will import or export the polymer granules. The first board resolution must be presented to the bank so that the bank can open the trade finance facility for irrevocable letter-of-credit and SWIFT transactions. If the company will operate a warehouse in Taiwan, the local municipal fire department must inspect the premises, and the company must obtain a fire safety facility inspection certificate before storing virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules.
required_dossiers: Business and corporate income tax registration forms
Bank account opening application and certified first board resolution
Principal place of business lease agreement
Fire safety equipment installation and inspection applications if warehousing
Customs registration application if import-export operations commence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau questions the business classification or the use of letter-of-credit instruments, the company shall submit the certified first board resolution, the procurement contract, and a written explanation of the trade flow. If the fire department refuses inspection clearance, the company must complete the listed fire safety corrections and request a reinspection within the period stated in the deficiency notice. Any adverse tax or fire ruling may be appealed through the applicable administrative appeal channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, in coordination with local municipal fire departments for fire safety, the Ministry of Environment for environmental obligations, and the competent local tax authority for business registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Unified Business Registration and Profit-Seeking Enterprise Registration, together with a Fire Safety Facility Inspection Certificate for any Taiwan warehouse storing commercial quantities of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules; no separate sectoral operating license is required for pure wholesale distribution under ISIC 4669.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (formerly Environmental Protection Administration), Taiwan, together with the local environmental protection bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from preparing a formal environmental impact assessment report for wholesale distribution and warehouse storage of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, provided the facility is not located in an environmentally sensitive area, does not handle substances classified as toxic chemical substances under the Toxic and Concerned Chemical Substances Control Act, and does not undergo any compounding, melting, extrusion, washing, or chemical reaction. If downstream processing of polymers is added, the activity will be reclassified and may require a category B preliminary environmental review or a category C full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For the exempt wholesale and warehousing operation, there shall be no process wastewater; any sanitary or stormwater discharge must meet Taiwan effluent standards with pH between 6.0 and 9.0, BOD5 below 30 mg/L, COD below 100 mg/L, and suspended solids below 30 mg/L. No VOC-emitting process equipment is permitted in the exempt configuration; any fugitive dust from bagging or silo transfer must remain below applicable ambient air quality standards. Any emergency diesel generator, if installed, must use fuel with sulfur content not exceeding 10 ppm and must comply with stationary source air pollution permitting thresholds if the capacity exceeds regulatory thresholds. Hazardous waste, including contaminated absorbents, waste oil, or spilled materials, must be handled by a licensed waste contractor under the Waste Disposal Act and accompanied by required manifests. Polyolefin scrap and off-spec granules are non-hazardous and must be recycled or disposed of through permitted local channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office and any warehouse must obtain a lawful building occupancy permit from the municipal government and must comply with the Taiwan Fire Services Act. The warehouse must pass a fire safety inspection covering fire extinguishers, sprinkler density, emergency lighting, exit signs, aisle width, storage height, and fire department access. The operator must submit an annual fire safety equipment maintenance report to the local fire department and implement a fire safety management plan. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the company must perform a workplace hazard assessment, provide first-aid equipment and trained personnel, maintain material safety data sheets for polyolefin dust, prevent dust accumulation, and ensure employees receive safe handling and emergency response training. The company must also participate in local civil defense self-protection arrangements, such as providing building occupant rosters and cooperating with municipal post-disaster inspections, if so required by the competent authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局) via the E-Tax Platform (电子税务局) and the electronic tax registration system administered by the STA; cross-border investment entities also interact with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for establishment filings and subsequently obtain the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: First incorporate the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise with the local branch of the State Administration for Market Regulation (Market Regulation Administration) to obtain the Business License and the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which serves as the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN). Then complete post-incorporation tax registration through the electronic tax authority system (E-Tax Platform) within 30 days of obtaining the Business License. The WFOE must file the Comprehensive Tax Registration Form, submit the SAMR Business License, articles of association, valid passport and residence permit copies of the legal representative, the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, and proof of registered address. Upon successful processing, the STA issues the tax registration status and creates the electronic taxpayer profile linked to the USCC, enabling monthly VAT, Corporate Income Tax, stamp duty and withholding filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for general corporate status. A Chinese WFOE limited liability company is fully subject to Entity-Level Taxation under the Corporate Income Tax Law at 25%; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available in the Chinese domestic tax system. The entity may elect to be recognised as a Foreign-Invested Enterprise with national treatment and must follow statutory CIT quarterly prepayment and annual final settlement procedures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (China Value-Added Tax) administered under the PRC VAT Law and its Implementing Rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a WFOE engaged in wholesale of petrochemical polymers, no registration threshold exemption applies because corporate entities are mandatory VAT taxpayers. General taxpayer compulsory status arises when annual sales of goods exceed RMB 5,000,000; since the entity will be registered as a general taxpayer, the standard rate of 13% applies to wholesale supply of petrochemical polymer granules. If small-scale registration were chosen, the threshold is RMB 5,000,000 annual turnover and the simplified collection rate is 3%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory Digital-Invoice (全电发票 / Electronic Invoice) system through the e-invoice platform of the STA, synchronised with the E-Tax Platform. B2B VAT invoices are issued electronically in real-time via official provincial electronic invoice systems, uploaded to the national electronic invoice clearing platform, and validated centrally. The system requires tax U-key authentication, digital stamps and blue/red-letter invoice controls. Since 2022, the nationwide 'Full Digitalised Electronic Invoice' pilot applies to new general taxpayers; taxpayers must use the official e-invoice generation interface, transmit invoice XML/PDF via API to the STA, comply with the electronic invoice number and digital cipher rules, and cannot issue unauthorised paper VAT special invoices. A live fiscal clearance machine is not used in mainland China; instead, real-time validation and central invoice reconciliation occur through the STA's Electronic Invoice Service Platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The wholesale export of bulk petrochemical polymers (virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules) to Taiwan qualifies for a 0% VAT export zero-rating and VAT refund status if the goods physically leave China customs territory and are exported abroad, including cross-strait exports to Taiwan. The exporter must be a VAT general taxpayer, must complete the official export customs declaration in its own name or via an approved export agency, must issue an ordinary commercial invoice supporting the export, must receive foreign currency payment, and must ensure the export proceeds are repatriated and verified. Qualifying digital services are not in scope because this entity conducts physical goods wholesale; zero-rating also requires that the goods are sold to a non-resident buyer for delivery abroad and that all customs procedures occur before the next VAT filing period, or within the statutory export declaration deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单 / Export Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill evidencing export from mainland China to Taiwan
Foreign Exchange Proceeds Verification (出口收汇核销单 / Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Record)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Receipt of Overseas Remittance confirming payment in USD or other foreign currency from the Taiwan buyer
Export VAT refund application form filed via the STA E-Tax Platform
Evidence of the export sales ledger in CIF/FOB terms matching the customs declaration value
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is closely scrutinised by the State Taxation Administration and the General Administration of Customs. If the exporter fails to substantiate the export declaration, cannot evidence physical exit, does not repatriate foreign exchange within the statutory deadline, or submits falsified invoices or customs declarations, the tax authority may disallow the 0% rate, recover the input VAT refunded, impose supplementary VAT and unpaid tax surcharge (0.05% daily), and charge a penalty ranging from 0.5 to 5 times the evaded tax under the PRC Tax Administration Law. In severe cases involving fraudulent VAT export refunds, a 50% to 500% fine applies and the matter may be referred for criminal liability for tax fraud, with imprisonment up to seven years; the entity may also face GST/CIT adjustment, blacklisting, and revocation of export tax refund credentials.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed-float, partially convertible foreign exchange system. The RMB is fully convertible for current-account transactions supported by genuine trade documents, but capital-account flows are subject to registration, approval, or quota controls. A Taiwan-invested WFOE may receive equity capital only after FDI registration with SAFE; the inward remittance is credited to a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account, and any conversion into RMB must be made through a licensed bank placing funds into a Settlement-Pending Account with restricted spending purposes verified by contracts and invoices. Profit and dividend repatriation to the Taiwan investor is legal but requires audited financial statements, enterprise income tax and withholding tax payment certificates, and confirmation of the original capital-investment registration. There is no statutory forced conversion of current-account export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in settlement accounts or convert through a designated bank at market rates. However, capital-account RMB convertibility remains constrained, particularly for foreign-currency outbound guarantees, repayment of external debt, and offshore investments, each of which requires a SAFE-registered underlying transaction. Treasury teams must therefore use licensed commercial banks and maintain a complete transaction dossier; offshore EMIs or informal channels are not acceptable under PRC AML and illegal cross-border payment rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Administration reform, exporters are no longer subject to a fixed mandatory surrender ratio; 100% of export foreign currency receipts may be retained in a foreign-currency current account or settled into RMB at market rates. The statutory obligation is to repatriate export proceeds through licensed banks into mainland China and to ensure the actual receipt date is consistent with the expected receipt date declared in the Goods Trade Monitoring System. Any export payment collected later than 90 days after the customs export date must be reported as a deferred receipt, and B-class or C-class enterprises face enhanced supervision and restricted payment methods, but no fixed percentage conversion requirement applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Contribution Account plus RMB Basic Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account plus General Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Capital Account plus Trade Settlement and Corporate Internet Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary treasury or clearing rail. China's PBOC and SAFE regulatory perimeter does not recognise offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex as licensed banks for domestic corporate account opening, RMB settlement, or foreign exchange clearing. They cannot receive WFOE equity capital, issue capital verification reports, or act as clearing banks for LCs or outward trade payments. At best, they could support immaterial ancillary merchant collections in limited offshore currencies, but all RMB clearing and cross-border flows involving the WFOE must pass through a licensed Chinese commercial bank. Therefore, the recommended approach is to build the entire corporate banking structure on Tier-1 domestic banks and avoid EMIs for compliance-critical flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a mainland China WFOE account opening, the legal representative or a person expressly authorised by a notarized board resolution must appear physically at the bank branch for the initial AML and know-your-customer interview. Remote digital onboarding is not sufficient for this enhanced-risk tier. If the legal representative is resident outside mainland China, the bank may accept a notarized and authenticated power of attorney with consular or cross-strait notarization, but the authorised local financial officer must still attend in person. Taiwan-issued corporate documents, identity documents, and seals require authentication and official Chinese translation before the bank will accept them, and the ultimate beneficial owner must be identified and verified to natural-person level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait corporate ownership structure and ultimate beneficial owner opacity, creating enhanced money-laundering and tax-transparency risk under PRC AML rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Taiwan registry record, incumbency certificate, notarized shareholder register, UBO declaration tracing through all natural persons, passports or national identity documents for all 10% or greater shareholders, articles of association, board resolution appointing the WFOE legal representative, cross-strait notarized authentication, and an organisational structure chart confirming commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk petrochemical bulk polymer trading without clear physical logistics, increasing the likelihood of over-invoicing, under-invoicing, phantom trades, or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file comprising signed purchase and sale contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, customs declarations, warehouse receipts, transport contracts, terminal storage records, HS code classifications, product specifications, and downstream sales invoices demonstrating that the same bulk polymer volume flows through genuine physical supply chains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure arising from polymer products potentially being diverted to embargoed jurisdictions or military end-uses, triggering bank screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party screening reports for all counterparties, ultimate consignees, shipping lines, financial institutions, and cargo details against United Nations, U.S. OFAC, EU, Taiwan, and PRC sanctions lists; vendor and customer end-use declarations; product-export certification confirming HS codes 3901 and 3902 classifications; transaction monitoring logs; and a written internal export-compliance and diversion-red-flag procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital contribution coming from a low-tax jurisdiction or an offshore holding vehicle, raising suspicion over illegal cross-border capital movement and avoidance of FDI registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the Taiwan investing entity, bank statements evidencing the lawful accumulation of remitted funds, tax payment certificates, FDI foreign exchange registration form, board resolutions approving the capital contribution, a group structure and substance memo explaining the economic purpose of each entity, and confirmation that no shell or conduit entity exists without real operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan investor must remit the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a licensed mainland bank. The remittance purpose must be stated as FDI equity subscription for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, referencing the WFOE's SAFE FDI registration certificate and unified social credit code. After physical credit, the receiving bank verifies the funds against the capital contribution table, records the transaction in SAFE's Capital Account Information System, and the statutory capital verification report is issued by a qualified certified public accountant in mainland China. If the funds are settled into RMB, they must move to a Settlement-Pending Account and each payment from that account must be supported by an underlying contract and invoice to prevent misuse of capital-account funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of international polymer purchases, the WFOE should use standard trade-clearing rails through its domestic Chinese bank. Open-account and advance payments are cleared by SWIFT MT103 with the correct SAFE goods-trade purpose code and supporting contract, invoice, and customs declaration. Large-value and term purchases should be structured through irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600, transmitted by MT700/MT707, with settlement through SWIFT MT103/MT202. Documentary collections under ICC URC522, payable at sight or by acceptance, are acceptable for transactions with established counterparties and lower-risk jurisdictions. If the supplier agrees to CNY settlement, cross-border RMB clearing through CIPS may be used, but USD-denominated flows should continue through the SWIFT network via the Tier-1 domestic bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts with licensed banks, limited to genuine trade payables or receivables supported by signed contracts, invoices, and customs documents, with maturities matching the LC or invoice tenors.

RMB/USD FX swaps for managing settlement-date liquidity and rebalancing cash flows arising from confirmed trade transactions, provided each swap is linked to an underlying registered current-account flow.

Currency options, including plain-vanilla call or put options with premium paid in real currency, used exclusively to hedge confirmed polymer purchase or sale exposures and not for speculative trading or levered exotic structures.

Boundary: non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing RMB are not permissible for onshore corporate entities because SAFE requires deliverable FX hedging with genuine transaction support; currency swaps are permissible only for SAFE-registered capital-account flows such as external debt or FDI-related treasury operations, with real principal exchange at maturity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Market Entity Annual Report / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June for the preceding calendar year; the e-filing portal closes at 24:00 Beijing time on 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing causes the company to be added to the List of Enterprises Operating under Abnormal Conditions. If the listing persists for three consecutive years, SAMR moves the enterprise to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, the legal representative is barred from acting as director, supervisor or senior manager for three years, and the business license may be administratively revoked after the deregistration procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the SAMR-hosted integrated foreign investment information reporting system, with data shared with the State Taxation Administration and SAFE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory annual window as the market-entity annual report: 1 January through 30 June each year for the prior year; beneficial-owner and shareholding information must be current as of 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An overdue or false foreign-investment report draws a statutory correction order; continued noncompliance may trigger administrative penalties, public credit-record punishment, denial of preferential FIE policies and potential restriction of cross-border capital settlement, ultimately including being struck from the list of valid foreign-invested enterprise records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Reconciliation and Settlement Return (Annual CIT Final Settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), competent local tax service center; supplementary copy to local financial department where mandated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after fiscal year-end: for a calendar-year WFOE, due no later than 31 May of the following year; first-year WFOEs may use the statutory annual period as approved.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late settlement attracts interest at the statutory daily rate of 0.05% on underpaid tax from 1 June, a monthly late-filing penalty for the return itself, and, where concealment is found, a monetary penalty of 50% to five times the evaded tax. Persistent nonpayment can lead to bank-account freezing, asset seizure, exit control and administrative revocation of the business license after an enforcement summons remains unsatisfied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent PRC-certified CPA firm; audit report filed with the competent finance and tax authorities as required under the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise implementing rules and retained at the statutory registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year WFOE, the audited annual accounting statements must be issued and submitted to the finance and tax authorities within four months after year-end, normally before 30 April; if the tax authority requires reconciliation, the audit file must support the annual declaration completed by 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit means the annual financial report is legally ineffective for shareholder approval and tax settlement; the company may be fined under the Accounting Law for preparing non-compliant financial reports, with direct penalties against the legal representative and financial officer, and the tax authority may reject the annual return and impose late-filing consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Corporate Registers, Beneficial Owner Information and Company Seal/Business Licence Maintenance Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR local registration authority for change-registration events; the company secretary or internal compliance officer for the on-site corporate registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no fixed annual renewal, but every change to shareholders, paid-in capital, directors, supervisors, legal representative, registered address, articles of association or beneficial-owner data must be submitted to SAMR within 30 days of the change; the statutory registers must be updated at the same time.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late change-registration creates a defective registry record that may render the resolution or equity transfer unopposable against third parties; SAMR can place the entity on the abnormal-operations list, impose administrative fines, and in extreme cases treat the failure as evidence of discontinuing business and initiate strike-off or deregistration of the enterprise.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Taiwan-invested WFOE engaged in wholesale distribution, an independent audit is mandatory without any size exemption. The mandatory audit is triggered if: (a) the entity is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, because the PRC WFOE implementation rules require the annual accounting statements to be examined and certified by a PRC-registered CPA; (b) total assets at the balance-sheet date exceed RMB 50 million; (c) annual operating turnover exceeds RMB 50 million; (d) the average annual headcount exceeds 300; (e) the company has related-party cross-border transactions with the Taiwan parent or any affiliate, requiring transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation and audit assurance; (f) the enterprise applies for any tax incentive, refund, VAT simplification or customs AEO treatment; or (g) the tax authority issues a written audit notice. When no quantitative trigger exists, the foreign-invested status alone still makes the audit compulsory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / China GAAP), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS. The WFOE is expected to prepare statutory financial statements in RMB on an accrual and going-concern basis; for this cross-border petrochemical trading model, full ASBE rather than the simplified Small Business Accounting Standards is required because of the Taiwan related-party relationship, foreign-investment reporting and audit expectations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Measures, the Taiwan-invested WFOE must report its beneficial-owner information to SAMR at formation and within 30 days after any change of ultimate natural-person ownership, control layer, or management control. The annual market-entity report filed with SAMR by 30 June acts as the annual confirmation of the current shareholding and investment structure. Any share transfer or paid-in-capital change must be registered with SAMR within 30 days of signing, and the internal register of members must be updated by the effective date; a thirty-day reporting window applies to equity transfers, foreign-investment information changes, and beneficial-owner updates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Management Personnel
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Encumbrances
Register of Beneficial Owners and Ultimate Controllers
Company Minute Book and Resolutions File
Transfer Ledger for Equity Interests and Capital Changes
Official Seal, Licence and Disclosure Records Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per annum for registered address, corporate secretary, mail handling and statutory register maintenance in a tier-1 Chinese city
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 per annum for the identified medium-risk petrochemical polymer wholesale WFOE, depending on transaction volume, intercompany balance complexity and required transfer pricing schedules

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China Corporate Income Tax Law imposes a 25% headline rate. Qualifying small low-profit enterprises (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million) may in practice enjoy a 5% effective rate through the 20% reduced rate plus additional deduction. Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises enjoy a 15% rate. R&D expenses qualifying under the Super Deduction may be deducted at 175% or 200%, but a pure wholesale distributor of petrochemical polymers is not automatically eligible and must establish statutory qualifications. No specific free-zone income-tax holiday covers the described WFOE unless the entity is registered in Hainan Free Trade Port and engages in encouraged industries. General tax-loss carryforward is 5 years for the WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary annual return is Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, General Class) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (Electronic Tax Administration e-Tax), together with the related party transaction disclosure schedules and supplementary forms. Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments are filed on Form A200000 through the same electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment is due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The annual final CIT return and payment are due no later than 31 May of the year following the tax year. Approval of extension is exceptional and interest may accrue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue: gross sales revenue from wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, including domestic sales and export sales to related and unrelated non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise all revenue at gross invoice value; do not net intercompany rebates or settlement discounts. For sales to the Taiwan-related party, apply the arm's length price and maintain contemporaneous comparability evidence. Omission of export revenue to an affiliated Taiwan buyer is an immediate transfer pricing audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs: cost of inventory sold, customs duties, freight, insurance, storage and directly attributable procurement costs for imported petrochemical pellets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all inbound purchases from a Taiwan related supplier with customs declarations, inspection reports, ocean or freight contracts, and a reliable comparability analysis. Inflated inward transfer prices create hidden outbound value and will be re-determined under Article 41 of the China CIT Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, service fees, and administrative recharges paid to the Taiwan parent are deductible only if real services were provided, evidenced by contracts, work papers and headcount documentation, and priced at arm's length. Payments to non-resident service providers may also carry withholding obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating and other items: asset impairment losses, changes in fair value, investment income, disposal gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany loans, related-party advances and guarantee balances. Interest income from the Taiwan affiliate must reflect the market rate at issuance. Any impairment or write-off of intercompany receivables must be supported by documentation of an actual credit loss and arm's length terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit: book profit before tax for the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The accounting profit should be consistent with the audited financial statements. If the WFOE shows persistent losses while the Taiwan affiliate shows significant profits from the same distribution chain, the tax bureau may disregard the structure or apply a transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation: add-ins, deduct-outs, disallowances, tax-exempt income, and after-tax losses from subsidiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment, unapproved donations, fines, penalties, and non-statutory impairment. When the WFOE pays royalties, interest or technical fees to Taiwan, any withholding tax borne by the WFOE is generally not deductible as its own income tax. Ensure the reconciliation is mapped to Schedule A105000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after offsetting prior-year losses and applying special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year statutory loss carryforward only for losses actually incurred in the WFOE. A shell WFOE with no commercial substance cannot transfer losses from the Taiwan parent. A significant change in ownership or business nature may forfeit loss carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT liability calculation: taxable income multiplied by 25%; then reduction for preferential rates and additional deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is not a qualified high-tech or small low-profit enterprise, use the headline 25% rate. Do not claim treaty reduced rates on intercompany fees in the annual CIT return; those reductions are handled through withholding tax procedures at payment time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE derives Taiwan-sourced income subject to Taiwan income tax, a foreign tax credit may be available against China CIT to the extent permitted by domestic law and the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement. Provide a credit calculation and foreign tax payment certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Schedule A105000, A105030, A105080 and Related Party Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing and related-party disclosure fields embedded in the annual return package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all related parties, including the Taiwan shareholder and affiliated suppliers/customers. State whether Local File or Master File thresholds are exceeded. If related-party tangible property turnover exceeds RMB 200 million in a year, attend to contemporaneous Local File preparation before the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / Withholding Tax and DTA Declaration Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of outbound dividend, interest, royalty or service payments to the non-resident Taiwan shareholder and related non-resident beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule is critical for the non-resident tax declaration: before remitting a dividend to the Taiwan shareholder, the WFOE must withhold 10% at the statutory rate, or apply the 5% dividend rate under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement only after receiving and retaining the Taiwanese Tax Residency Certificate and evidencing the 25% direct holding and beneficial ownership. In all cases the standard non-resident withholding return must be filed within the statutory period after the payment becomes due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts an administrative penalty under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Administration Law of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, rising to RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 for a serious violation. Late payment of CIT accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax. False or fraudulent returns, including deliberately understating revenue or fabricating costs, fall under Article 63 and cause recovery of underpaid tax, late interest, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Where the false filing is criminal, Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law permits imprisonment and fines; the legal representative and financial officer can be individually prosecuted when they planned or executed the fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: Confirm that the Taiwan recipient is a tax resident of Taiwan for the period in which the dividend is paid and obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) bearing the current year. Step 2: Confirm that the Taiwan shareholder directly owns at least 25% of the WFOE paid-in capital for the continuous holding period required under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Tax Cooperation; only then may the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate apply. Step 3: Establish beneficial ownership under STA Announcement 2018 No. 35: the Taiwan shareholder must have substantive business, employees, premises, decision-making authority, and not act as a conduit to another jurisdiction. Step 4: Submit to the Chinese competent tax authority a written DTA relief application, the TRC, audited financial statements of the Taiwan company, a beneficial ownership declaration, a shareholding structure chart, and a commitment to report substantial changes. Step 5: After the tax authority accepts the reduced-rate application, the WFOE withholds at 5% and issues the non-resident withholding tax certificate. If the reduced rate is not accepted, withhold at 10% and the Taiwan shareholder may claim refund of the excess through Chinese tax authorities within the applicable limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under PRC domestic law, interest and royalties paid by a resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China are each subject to 10% withholding tax. Under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, the maximum withholding rate for interest and royalties is also 10% of the gross payment, provided the Taiwan recipient is the beneficial owner. Royalties for patents, know-how, trademarks and software use must be arm's length and supported by licence registration and substance evidence. Interest paid to a Taiwan related party is also subject to thin-capitalisation limitation; debt-to-equity ratios must be respected. Without treaty relief or beneficial ownership, the statutory 10% WHT is collected at source by the WFOE as withholder.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million annual aggregate related-party tangible-asset transfers; RMB 100 million annual aggregate related-party intangible-asset transfers; RMB 100 million annual aggregate related-party financial-asset transfers; RMB 40 million annual aggregate related-party service transactions. A Master File is required where the group's related-party revenue reaches RMB 1 billion and other statutory conditions are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations registration regime, but the substance doctrine is embedded in Article 47 of the CIT Law, the General Anti-Avoidance Rules, and the beneficial-owner tests under STA Announcement 2018 No. 35. The WFOE must demonstrate real core income-generating activities: procurement, inventory management, marketing, sales contracting, logistics coordination and risk control in China. The Taiwan shareholder claiming 5% dividend relief must itself perform the CIGA related to its shareholding and be the true economic owner of the shares. A letterbox Taiwan company, or a WFOE that merely creates paper invoices while the real trading functions occur outside China, will be denied treaty benefits and may be treated as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Deliberate False CIT Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE files an annual CIT return that omits related-party export revenues to the Taiwan buyer, inflates inventory costs through fake purchase invoices, or books fictitious logistics and warehouse expenses, thereby reducing taxable profit and causing underpayment of China corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law: the tax authority recovers the underpaid tax plus late-payment surcharge and imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax. Serious evasion involving substantial amounts is criminal under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, with fines and imprisonment for persons directly responsible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the statutory legal representative may have the corporate veil pierced under PRC Company Law if they abused the limited liability entity to conceal assets from tax authorities; courts may order civil restitution of diverted funds, freeze bank accounts, and restrict travel. The director in charge of accounting and taxation may be blacklisted as a seriously dishonest taxpayer, subjected to an exit ban, disqualified from serving as director, and sentenced to imprisonment for up to seven years for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Missing Contemporaneous Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE buys virgin polyethylene and polypropylene from a Taiwan related supplier at artificially high prices and resells at artificially low prices to a Taiwanese distributor, leaving the Chinese entity with no profit or continuous losses, while the WFOE omits to prepare a Local File and Master File although statutory related-party annual turnover thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41 and 47 of the PRC CIT Law and STA Announcement 2016 No. 42 allow the tax authority to re-determine taxable income using the arm's length principle, impose interest and late-payment surcharges, and apply penalties for failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation. If the mispricing is characterised as fraud, penalties may equal 50% to 500% of the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signed false transfer pricing documentation or instructed the financial team to conceal intercompany transactions may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax adjustments where the structure is held to be an abuse; the company may be blacklisted and the director restrained from obtaining tax clearance for outbound travel or asset sales. Serious deliberate mispricing with forged comparables can expose officers to criminal liability for tax evasion or document fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Conduit and Abusive DTA Relief / Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan shareholder is a shell entity with no employees, office, business activities or real assumption of risk, created solely to hold 25% or more of the WFOE and to claim the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, while the true beneficiary is a third-country principal that enjoys treaty-shopping benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: STA Announcement 2018 No. 35 denies beneficial-owner status and the tax authority disregards the treaty benefit, reimposing the statutory 10% withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties, together with late-payment interest and penalties. Application of the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the CIT Law can also cause recharacterisation of the financing and service arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shadow directors and shareholders who caused incorporation of the shell to evade tax may have the corporate veil pierced, with obligations to refund the preferential tax avoided and to satisfy unpaid corporate liabilities from personal assets. Taiwan and Chinese administrative authorities may place the entity on a tax violation blacklist, ban the legal representative from leaving the jurisdiction, and in cases of fraudulent tax refund or intentional evasion, the responsible individuals may face criminal imprisonment and criminal fines.
